name: Bento
one_liner: A PowerPoint alternative in one HTML file; edit, present and share with only a browser.

text.why: While office documents have moved behind cloud logins, Bento takes the other path. The deck, fonts, images, charts and the full editor travel in one .bento.html file, and on save the file rewrites its own data block (File System Access API, with a download fallback). The document sits as readable JSON near the top of the file, so an AI agent or any other tool can edit it in place.
text.take: The point is that the file is the software; anything with a browser opens it.
build: Ship a company template as a .bento.html file that colleagues can edit and present with nothing installed, or write a script that generates decks from data because the document is plain JSON.

who.role: Small teams that trade decks often
who.situation: share slides the other side can open without installing anything

who.role: Developers driving documents with AI agents
who.situation: generate slides by editing the JSON block
presentations that stay as a local file

start.text: 1. Open https://bento.page/slides in a browser (the whole app, running on a starter deck)
2. Or download the file: https://bento.page/releases/slides/Bento_Slides.bento.html (~560 KB per the README, ~710 KB per the site; no account, no installer)

caveat: MIT licence (bundled reveal.js, Moveable and Selecto are MIT; typefaces OFL). Editing is desktop-first; phones are for viewing and presenting, per the README. Known trade-off: undo during live collaboration is snapshot-based and can revert a collaborator's concurrent edit to the same property; the sync relay is optional. Free.
